title: E-commerce Cart
summary: Add items, apply discounts, and turn a cart into an order.
problem: Design a shopping cart: customers add and remove products, apply coupons, see a total with tax and shipping, and check out into an order.
functional: Add, remove and change the quantity of an item
Apply at most one coupon, with different rule types (percentage, fixed amount, free shipping)
Compute subtotal, discount, tax, shipping and total
Checkout creates an order and reserves stock
nonFunctional: New discount rules must be addable without editing the cart
Prices at checkout must equal prices shown in the cart
constraints: One currency; payment is out of scope
deliverables: A class diagram (Mermaid or an uploaded image) with the relationships between classes
The responsibility of each class in a sentence
The design patterns you used and where, or why you used none
Optional: code for the central class and one method of each
hints: The cart should not know how a discount is calculated: give that to a rule.
An order is a snapshot: copy the prices at checkout, do not point at live products.
reference:
```mermaid
classDiagram
  class Cart { items +add(product, qty) +remove(product) +total() Money +checkout() Order }
  class CartItem { product quantity }
  class DiscountRule { <<interface>> +apply(cart) Money }
  class PercentageOff
  class FixedAmountOff
  class FreeShipping
  class PricingService { +price(cart) PriceBreakdown }
  class TaxPolicy { <<interface>> +tax(cart) Money }
  class ShippingPolicy { <<interface>> +shipping(cart) Money }
  class Order { lines total placedAt }
  Cart o-- CartItem
  DiscountRule <|-- PercentageOff
  DiscountRule <|-- FixedAmountOff
  DiscountRule <|-- FreeShipping
  PricingService --> DiscountRule
  PricingService --> TaxPolicy
  PricingService --> ShippingPolicy
  Order *-- OrderLine
  Cart --> PricingService
  Cart ..> Order
```

- `PricingService` composes tax, shipping and the coupon's `DiscountRule` (strategy); the cart only asks for a breakdown.
- Checkout re-prices the cart, and if the total differs from what the shopper last saw it stops and asks them to confirm, so "checkout equals what was shown" holds. It then builds an `Order` from a snapshot of the line prices (`OrderLine`) and reserves stock: in the same transaction if stock lives in the same database, otherwise as a reservation that is released if the order cannot be completed.
- Quantities and money are value objects that cannot be negative.
